SpaceX passes first lockup expiry test with US$500 bil rally
article:
(Aug 13): Since SpaceX went public in June, Wall Street had been dreading Aug 6, when the first lockup preventing early investors from selling the stock expired and millions of shares were set to flood the market.

SpaceX shares have been on a tear since the lockup ended, soaring 35% in just five sessions, adding roughly US$500 billion in market capitalisation, and vaulting back over their US$135 initial public offering (IPO) price. The surge bucked concerns about an impending wave of selling and gave investors optimism that future expirations won’t be as painful as feared.

“We’ve gotten through the big hurdle, which was the unknown,” said Andrew Plum, managing partner and investment committee head at Loxahatchee Capital, which holds SpaceX shares. “It’s like the market discounts a negative event, maybe too much, as it’s waiting for that information to come to pass. And then it’s usually not as bad as what was discounted or as expected.”

SpaceX shares were down 2.4% in early trading Thursday.

See also: S&P 500 closes near record high on tame inflation

Elon Musk’s space, satellite and artificial intelligence (AI) company has had a wild ride in the stock market since pricing its record US$86 billion IPO on June 11. The shares took off in their first days of trading before reversing direction and shedding more than US$1 trillion in market value through early August. The lockup expiration was supposed to be another hazard, but it turned out to be a blip.

“If the stock was US$225, I would guess that it would have succumbed to the trend,” said Gene Munster, managing partner at Deepwater Asset Management, which holds SpaceX shares. He described his firm as in “brace mode” leading up to the expiration as they waited to see what transpired.

The process for unlocking SpaceX shares is different than what usually happens after an IPO, where insiders are generally restricted from selling for 180 days. Considering the company’s size and its potential ability to shock the market, SpaceX’s management and bankers spread out the expirations with a nine-stage structure.

See also: US stocks rise as inflation keeps Fed ‘at bay’, spurs tech rally

This lockup was the biggest one, with 911.5 million shares coming available, more than were sold in the IPO. The next expiration is on Aug 20, triggering the release of as many as 319 million shares, or 7% of the total amount of stock subject to selling restrictions. Similar 7% blocks will become available over the next few months before Musk’s 6.4 billion shares are unlocked in June 2027.

SpaceX shares plunged 14% on the day before the expiration, but the culprit actually appears to be the company’s first earnings report, and specifically its higher-than-expected capital expenditures for AI. However, the results also contained some good news, including a large beat in revenue and a better-than-expected loss per share. Those figures were likely another catalyst in the stock’s runup since then.

“Once investors realised after that first day that it’s not going to go into free fall, then they realised they could kind of go back and reassess what happened in the quarter and realise that things are moving along,” Munster said.

Musk, as he so often does, also offered some bold predictions on the earnings call. In particular, he said he expects SpaceX’s revenue to reach a more than US$100 billion annual run rate by the end of the year and US$1 trillion in revenue by 2030 or possibly 2029.

“The earnings release was pretty surprising to the upside, and I think that’s the antidote to shares coming on the market,” Plum said. “You can have very good financial news coming from the company that’s going to attract new buyers at these levels, which will allow those shares to exit at a reasonable price and not to put too much pressure on the stock.”

Some investors weren’t particularly surprised that SpaceX shares behaved differently than other stocks after the lockup expiration. While these events generally pressure the shares involved, Musk’s popularity may have changed the game.

“I would assume that the initial early base of space investors are not loyal to market fundamentals, they’re loyal to Elon and his dream,” said David Wagner, a portfolio manager at Aptus Capital Advisors, which owns SpaceX shares. “This investor base may be stickier than what you would assume because it’s a bet on Elon and not a bet on fundamental earnings, execution and free cash flow execution over short periods of time.”

That the stock was trading well below the IPO price heading into the lockup expiration might’ve also helped, according to Munster. He anticipates a similar trading pattern to possibly emerge around future lockup expirations — with shares falling ahead of the release, then gaining after — as long as insiders don’t rush to unload their stakes.

The bottom line for SpaceX investors is expect the stock to experience some big swings as more shares reach the market and the narrative surrounding the company evolves.

“I expect this stock to be volatile and go between fear of a story that is promising but is several years out in terms of cash flow, and greed when investors get excited about [Musk’s] vision and the stunning promise,” said Rhys Williams, chief strategist at Wayve Capital Management. “Bulls can dream the dream. And bears will focus on a stunning amount of capex.”

title: DeepSeek increases prices for AI services by multiple times
article:
(Aug 13): DeepSeek is steeply raising the prices for its flagship V4 models, bringing the low-cost provider’s rates closer to those of major artificial intelligence (AI) rivals.

A new peak-hour pricing will increase the Chinese company’s rates by more than four times from the current levels, according to a post on its website on Thursday. The price increases will take effect on Aug 16.

Going forward, users will pay US$1.32 for one million output tokens during peak hours, and half that during off-peak hours, for the DeepSeek-V4-Flash model. That’s up from US$0.28 for one million tokens previously.

The increase still leaves DeepSeek’s pricing below that of some of its main competitors. Anthropic PBC’s state-of-the-art Fable 5 service sets that pricing at US$50. DeepSeek gave an advance warning last week that it would hike prices, without specifying the exact increases.

DeepSeek’s V4-Pro model will cost US$3.96 for one million tokens at peak hours and half that at non-peak hours, it said. That’s up from the current US$0.87 per million tokens.

The Hangzhou-based AI lab said it’s revising and adjusting the pricing “to allocate resources more reasonably”. The dynamic pricing strategy is designed to encourage developers and enterprises to shift their work to less congested periods.

See also: South Korean stocks up 22% in 10 days as chip rally regains steam

DeepSeek’s strategy has sparked a global debate in recent weeks over the cost of high-performing AI tools. Its pricing has been so far out of the usual range for AI models that it has prompted the idea of a DeepSeek “death zone”, where costlier or less capable models would be obviated. It’s also raised questions about the initial public offering plans of OpenAI and Anthropic because of the risks the firm poses to their profits and business models.

DeepSeek is in the middle of a massive fundraising and has begun preparations for an initial public offering as soon as this year, Bloomberg has reported. Founder Liang Wenfeng will for the first time need to balance investor expectations, rapid market expansion and the intense capital demands of building out costly computing infrastructure.

title: Seatrium signs LOI with Golar for 3rd FLNG conversion
article:
Two weeks after updating at its 1HFY2026 briefing that it was targeting a “leading share” in gas projects, Mainboard-listed Seatrium has announced that it has entered into a Letter of Intent (LOI) with repeat customer Golar LNG to advance a potential third floating liquified natural gas (FLNG) conversion project.

Under the arrangement, Seatrium and Golar will work together to advance technical design development and project definition activities, with the objective of finalising an engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract in 2H2026. An upfront consideration will support Seatrium’s activities relating to the LOI to be undertaken prior to EPC contract execution.

Previously, Seatrium had converted two LNG carriers (LNGC) into FLNGs for Golar. These two vessels, FLNG Hilli Episeyo with 2.4 million tonnes per annum (mpta) capacity and FLNG Gimi with 2.7 mtpa capacity, are the world’s only two operational FLNG vessels converted from LNGCs.

Marlin Khiew, executive vice president of Seatrium Energy (Projects), says: “Golar's continued confidence in Seatrium reflects our proven track record in delivering complex floating gas solutions. Leveraging the experience gained from FLNG Hilli Episeyo and FLNG Gimi, we aim to enhance standardisation through a series-build approach that delivers greater execution certainty, speed to market and cost effectiveness.”

Golar chief technical officer Morten Skjong adds: “We are excited to continue our 20+ years’ partnership with Seatrium by developing potential further FLNG projects. With the FLNG Hilli on its way to Seatrium for vessel upgrades ahead of its 20-year charter in Argentina, we will seek to further expand our FLNG collaboration through today’s announced LOI.”

In addition to the two LNGC-to-FLNG conversions, Seatrium has executed over 90% of global FSRU and floating storage unit (FSU) conversions and has developed FLNG-X, a proprietary, modular, and scalable newbuild FLNG design. In total, Seatrium is competing for gas-related business worth around $11 billion.

See also: Reclaims Global secures $19.89 mil in new contracts in 2QFY2026

Shares in Seatrium fell one cent, or 0.5%, to $2.14 on Aug 13.

title: Nam Cheong’s 1HFY2026 net profit jumps 82.9% y-o-y to above RM164 mil
article:
For 1HFY2026 ended June 30, Sarawak-based shipbuilder and charterer Nam Cheong reported 82.9% y-o-y higher net profit of over RM164 million, on revenue of around RM348 million, which is 25.2% y-o-y higher than 1HFY2025. No interim dividend was declared.

Gross profit declined 3% to approximately RM137 million and overall gross margin narrowed by 11.4 percentage points to 39.4%, reflecting a revenue mix from the shipbuilding segment as well as a lower y-o-y gross margin for the chartering segment.

Other income rose to around RM103 million for 1HFY2026 from RM6.3 million a year ago. This was mostly due to a vessel disposal gain of RM101 million. The vessel sale is part of Nam Cheong’s debt repayment and fleet reprofiling strategies, in which sale proceeds go towards funding newbuild.

Selling and administrative expenses rose 60% to RM42.9 million on higher staff and marketing costs as chartering operations and in-house newbuilding activity expanded.

On a segmental basis for the half-year, shipbuilding contributed RM89.7 million of revenue, the first time in six years that the segment recorded income. This was from the sale and delivery of one vessel and progressive revenue recognition on vessels under construction. Gross margin for the shipbuilding segment was 25%.

Revenue from vessel chartering declined 7.1% to around RM259 million. This was attributed to lower utilisation of the accommodation vessels which was cushioned by the higher overall vessel utilisation rate of 65% in 1HFY2026 as compared to 58% in 1HFY2025. Chartering gross margin declined to 44.3% from 50.8% a year ago, mainly due to higher operating costs for vessels deployed in the Middle East and the lower utilisation of accommodation vessels.

See also: Choo Chiang’s 1HFY2026 earnings jumped 54.7% y-o-y to $6.5 mil; declares interim dividend of 1.2 cents per share

As of end-June, 71% of the fleet, or 25 of the 35 vessels, are on long-term charters. This is in line with Nam Cheong’s target of 70% long-term charter coverage, which supports its aim to strike a “healthy” balance between long-term visible recurring income, and opportunities to capture upsides in the spot market.

As at June 30, the company held cash and bank balances of RM226 million compared to RM193 million as at Dec 31. Customer payments contributed to the higher cash holdings. The company repaid a portion of its debts, with borrowings down from end-2025's RM425 million to end-June’s RM340 million. Consequently, Nam Cheong’s net gearing ratio decreased from 0.27 times at end-2025 to 0.10 times as at end-June.

The company notes higher levels of offshore spending for the Malaysian market. It also observes that offshore activity and the demand for offshore support vessels (OSVs) also remain “strong”.

See also: UMS Integration 2QFY2026 earnings up 89% y-o-y; 1HFY2026 up 66%

CEO Leong Seng Keat says that operating both shipbuilding and ship chartering businesses affords Nam Cheong with the flexibility to either build vessels inhouse expand its fleet or sell them in the market when opportune.

He adds, “Looking ahead, we are on track to add 5 vessels to our fleet by the end of the year, and are encouraged by the elevated level of enquiries for shipbuilding.”

title: EGP Energy 1HFY2026 net profit soars 180% y-o-y to $6.07 mil in maiden results
article:
For 1HFY2026 ended June 30, newly-listed EGP Energy Corporation reported 180% y-o-y rise in patmi to $6.07 million, on revenue of $30.7 million, which is a 157% increase from the previous corresponding period. No interim dividend was declared.

Gross profit rose 227% y-o-y to $10.1 million, outpacing growth in cost of sales which rose 133% y-o-y to $20.6 million. The stronger performance was attributed to higher revenue from the transmission and distribution (T&D) and maintenance and services (M&S) segments.

Segmentally, the T&D segment recorded half-year revenue of $20.8 million, up 156% y-o-y. This was mainly due to revenue recognised from new T&D projects that commenced during 1HFY2026 as well as from projects that commenced in late FY2025 and progressed substantially during 1HFY2026.

Meanwhile, the M&S segment saw its revenue grow nearly 160% y-o-y to $9.9 million due to the commencement of a new project during 1HFY2026 and an increase of approximately $2.0 million from the provision of ad-hoc services during the six months under review.

As at June 30, cash and bank balances stood at $27.1 million and the company had zero bank borrowings. Net asset value is 25.08 cents.

As of Aug 13, EGP Energy’s order book stood at $296.2 million, with projects are slated for progressive completion through 2031, providing revenue visibility.

See also: Megachem’s 1HFY2026 earnings surge 167.9% y-o-y to $4.6 mil; declares interim dividend of 0.5 cents per share

The company is “optimistic” about its business prospects over the next 12 months. Its growing order book, established customer relationships, experienced management team and strengthened balance sheet following the successful completion of its IPO, which raised net proceeds of $27.4 million, supports its outlook.

“Backed by our track record, longstanding customer relationships and experienced project team, we will continue to pursue tender opportunities that play to our technical strengths and meet our targeted returns,” says CEO Frankie Fan. “With the funds raised from our recent IPO, we are well-positioned to accelerate our growth plans, including strategic partnerships, joint ventures and acquisitions, and to expand into selected regional markets where our expertise gives us a clear edge.”

Shares in EGP Energy dipped 0.5 cents, or 0.7%, to close at 77 cents on Aug 13. Since joining the Mainboard of the Singapore stock exchange on July 29, the stock has surged 51% from its IPO price of 51 cents.

title: JLR owner misses profit estimate stung by luxury unit slack
article:
(Aug 13): Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd, the parent of Jaguar Land Rover, reported a lower-than-expected quarterly profit, as the weakness in its UK luxury unit offset strong sales in India.

Net income fell 80% to 7.75 billion rupees in the three months ended June 30, the automaker said in a filing on Thursday. It missed the average profit estimate of 11.8 billion rupees compiled from a Bloomberg survey of brokerages.

Revenue was at 958 billion rupees, beating analyst estimates This metric for JLR slipped 9.5% to £5.97 billion while pretax income for the unit was £109 million.

Volumes and revenue for JLR was impacted by “temporary supply constraints, including a fire at a major component supplier at the start of the quarter, market disruption linked to the conflict in the Middle East, and the planned wind down of outgoing Jaguar models ahead of the launch of Jaguar Type 01,” Tata Motors PV said in the post-earnings investor presentation.

An employee polishes paint on the bodywork of a Range Rover sports utility vehicle at the Jaguar Land Rover vehicle manufacturing plant in Solihull. (Photo by Bloomberg)

See also: London’s billionaire home sales thrive as millionaire deals lag

Global geopolitical developments and luxury segment trends continue to be key factors to watch, the Indian company said in a statement. On the domestic front, it will focus on revenue growth while also aiming to reduce costs, it added.

The earnings point to continuing headwinds for the carmaker, especially at JLR — Britain’s largest carmaker — as it recovers from a year when its profit was almost entirely wiped out due to the hit from US tariffs, a demand slump in China and a crippling cyberattack that roiled production last September for weeks.

The broader Tata Group is also facing a bout of uncertainty around its capital spending plans after its chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran resigned this week.

See also: New PM Burnham walks back proposal to lift UK income tax threshold

JLR reported wholesale volumes of 79,300 units for the quarter, down 9.2% from a year ago, while the retail sales at 80,000 units, had slipped 15.3%.

The luxury carmaker showcased a prototype of the upcoming Ranger Rover Sport Electric SUV earlier this month, a precursor to the commercial rollout of the brand’s first range of electric vehicles in the coming months.

The company is preparing for an important transition year at JLR, chief financial officer Dhiman Gupta said in a statement. Supply constraints, elevated commodity costs and foreign exchange rates continued to impact performance in the June quarter, he added.

The automaker aims to expand its India market share from 14.2% to 20% by March 2031, aided by the launch of six new models and more than 20 product refreshes. It also expects JLR to contribute US$45 billion to US$50 billion of revenue by March 2031. The maker of luxury sedans and sport utility vehicles will add more hybrid SUVs to bolster the US sales, becoming the latest automaker to temper its electric ambitions.
